title: Prom and Group Chat
premise: Edmund Villalobos, the only out kid in the dying town of Halloway Springs, has survived high school by keeping her head down and her group chat 'the prom committee' full of jokes nobody takes seriously. But when history teacher Ms. Okafor pairs her with her nemesis, star athlete and school board golden boy Cole Brandt, for a semester project on local archives, they unearth a 1998 fire that killed three students and a cover-up implicating the very families who still run the town—including Cole's. As Edmund's anonymous posts about the archive go viral, the board retaliates: her scholarship, her mother's job, and finally her safety are all on the table. In the end, Edmund chooses to testify at the centennial prom-turned-town-hall, trading her invisibility for the truth, while Cole must decide whether his name protects him or indicts him.
about_author: Ines Reyes grew up in a town so small the yearbook doubled as the phone book, and she has been writing about kids who refuse to disappear ever since. She teaches creative writing to teenagers and insists every story should have at least one group chat in it.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred People, One Closet Door
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A wry tour of Halloway Springs through Edmund's morning: the diner, the mural of the 1998 fire, the hallway where everyone knows her name but no one uses it right. She narrates her survival strategy—invisibility—and we see how exhausting 'fine' really is. Beat: lonely defiance.

chapters.title: The Prom Committee
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Introduce the group chat: four friends who plan a prom that may never happen because the school can't afford one. Banter establishes each voice and hides Edmund's real fear—that after graduation there'll be nothing left of her here. Beat: warmth with an undertow.

chapters.title: Assigned Seating
chapters.summary: Ms. Okafor announces semester partners for the local history capstone; Edmund draws Cole Brandt, who once stood by while his friends trashed her locker. Their first meeting is all barbed politeness. Edmund notices Cole flinches when she mentions the fire mural. Beat: reluctant collision.

chapters.title: Basement of the Historical Society
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. The pair digs through water-damaged boxes and finds a sealed file labeled HALLOWAY HIGH — INCIDENT, redacted almost entirely. Cole knows something about the seal procedure; he won't say what. Beat: first crack in the armor.

chapters.title: Group Chat, 11:47 PM
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, told partly in chat logs. She floats the discovery to her friends; one urges caution, another dares her. Her mom comes home exhausted from the mill—the same mill owned by a board family. Beat: the price of curiosity becomes concrete.

chapters.title: Cole's Version of Fine
chapters.summary: Cole's POV. At Sunday dinner, his father—a school board member—rehearses talking points about the upcoming centennial prom. Cole realizes the family legend about his uncle, a 'hero' of the fire, doesn't match a photo he finds in the archive box. Beat: inherited guilt.

chapters.title: The Redaction Pattern
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Working late in the library, they map which names were blacked out across documents: always the same five families, including both of theirs. They agree to a fragile truce—find the truth, then decide together what to do. Beat: enemies become co-conspirators.

chapters.title: Homecoming Interference
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At homecoming, a board member corners Edmund with a smile and a warning about 'troublemakers.' Her friends notice she's spending time with Cole; the group chat fractures over loyalty and suspicion. Beat: social cost arrives early.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: Cole's POV. Following a lead, they track down Ruthie Calloway, a former student now living outside town, who was in the building the night of the fire. She slams the door—but not before saying, 'Ask them why the alarms didn't ring.' Beat: dread sharpens into purpose.

chapters.title: Anonymous Goes Viral
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Someone—Edmund swears it wasn't her—posts scans from the archive to a town Facebook page. The school goes into lockdown mode; Ms. Okafor is suspended pending 'review.' Edmund feels the net closing around whoever leaked. Beat: momentum turns dangerous.

chapters.title: Interrogation Light
chapters.summary: Cole's POV. His father confronts him with printouts of the group chat—someone screenshotted their private messages. Cole lies badly. He realizes the chat itself is evidence, and that trust between him and Edmund is now a liability someone will exploit. Beat: paranoia blooms.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Ruthie finally talks: the alarm system had been disconnected for renovation insurance reasons; three kids died in the east stairwell; the board settled quietly and rewrote the memorial plaque. She gives them a name—the custodian who was ordered to cut the wires. Beat: grief made specific.

chapters.title: The Custodian's Daughter
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The custodian died broke and blamed; his daughter, now the school secretary, has kept his work log for twenty-five years. She agrees to hand it over only if Edmund promises the truth won't be 'another thing this town eats.' Beat: stewardship of memory.

chapters.title: Prom Is Cancelled
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The board cancels the centennial prom citing 'safety concerns,' killing the group chat's year-long dream. Her friends turn on her: your project did this. Edmund, alone, nearly deletes everything. Beat: lowest point, isolation complete.

chapters.title: What Cole Knew All Along
chapters.summary: Cole's POV. Confession chapter: Cole found the incident file months ago during a board internship and said nothing—his silence bought his father's approval and a college recommendation. He tells Edmund, expecting to lose her. Beat: shame spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The Vote in the Chat
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, chat-log heavy. Instead of expelling Cole from their lives, the group chat votes—messily, angrily—to finish it together. They map the evidence chain: work log, Ruthie's testimony, redaction pattern, Cole's affidavit. Beat: chosen family reassembles.

chapters.title: Break-In at the Board Office
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The original unredacted incident report is locked in the district office before Monday's records purge. A tense late-night entry—Cole's key card, Edmund's lock-picking from a library book—ends with sirens and a near capture. They get photocopies, not originals. Beat: adrenaline and sacrifice.

chapters.title: Charges
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund is suspended and charged with trespass; her mother loses shifts at the mill. Facing expulsion days before graduation, Edmund must choose: accept a quiet deal to stay silent, or request a public hearing—which, by town charter, must be held at the centennial event. Beat: the trap becomes a stage.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for the Truth
chapters.summary: Cole's POV. Cole goes to his father privately and gives him one chance to resign and confess before the hearing. His father threatens disownment; Cole leaves the house anyway, taking the family's old photo album as evidence. Beat: severing the inheritance.

chapters.title: Centennial Prom
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The town gathers under paper lanterns; the board plans a whitewashed ceremony. Mid-speech, Edmund takes the microphone—not a rant, but the names of the three students read aloud, then the evidence, page by page, with Ruthie standing beside her. Beat: climax, voice at last.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unredacted
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Fallout in fast cuts: state investigation, two board resignations, the deal withdrawn because it no longer matters. The plaque is re-carved with all three names and the custodian's. Some friendships don't recover; the town doesn't forgive. Beat: costly victory.

chapters.title: The Group Chat Renames Itself
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, final chat log. Graduation day. The chat changes its name from 'prom committee' to something new—they're staying in touch past the town's borders. Edmund writes one last message: not fine, not invisible, finally herself. Beat: resolution, identity claimed.
